name: ProactBench
description: ProactBench is a benchmark for measuring conversational proactivity in multi-turn LLM dialogues. It decomposes proactivity into three phase-tied trigger types (Emergent, Critical, Recovery) and uses a three-agent evaluation architecture (Planner, User Agent, Evaluated Model) with information asymmetries that defend against rubric leakage, post-hoc rationalisation, style-confounded scoring, and information dumps. The corpus contains 198 curated dialogues with 624 trigger points across 5 persona categories and 24 communication styles drawn from the Communication Styles Inventory (CSI).
citeAs: @inproceedings{anonymous2026proactbench, title={ProactBench: Beyond What The User Asked For}, author={Anonymous}, booktitle={Under review at NeurIPS 2026}, year={2026}}
rai:dataCollection: Dialogues are synthetically generated by a three-agent pipeline. Personas are sampled from Nemotron-Personas-USA (NVIDIA, CC-BY-4.0). For each (persona, category) pair, a Planner LLM generates a proactive scenario with a hidden goal, explicit surface request, implicit anchors, and ideal trajectory. Scenarios are expanded into turn-by-turn blueprints under each of 24 CSI communication styles. Blueprints pass an independent-LLM-judge audit (different model family from the Planner) before inclusion. The full three-agent loop then runs once per validated blueprint to produce the final dialogue corpus. See the paper Section 3 and the README for full pipeline details.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Trigger points are scored at curation time by the User Agent stepping out of persona to evaluate the model's response against the Planner-authored rubric (PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL). Rubrics are committed prospectively at turn t before the model has responded, evaluated at turn t+1 after the response is generated. Each evaluation includes a verbatim evidence quote and a free-text rationale. A planned human-validation study (n=60 trigger points, 8 annotators, 3 raters per item) is documented in the paper Appendix and will be used to validate the automated judge.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Per-trigger-type pass rates and weighted scores (PASS=1.0, PARTIAL=0.5, FAIL=0.0) are reported across 16 evaluated models in the paper. A judge-swap ablation across three judges (GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7, Kimi-K2.6) shows pairwise Cohen's kappa of 0.35-0.46 on overall trigger labels, with model rankings preserved (Spearman rho 0.64-0.89).
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dialogues that fail to complete the minimum 5-turn requirement or that fail blueprint validation are excluded from the corpus. The released corpus has 198 dialogues that all complete >=5 turns with at least 2 trigger points each.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be hosted at an anonymous URL during peer review (HuggingFace Datasets after acceptance, with the same Apache-2.0 license). Updates and corrections will be tracked via the GitHub repository's release tags.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating large language models on conversational proactivity; comparing model behaviour at different conversational phases (Emergent / Critical / Recovery); studying robustness to user communication style variation; calibration of LLM-as-judge agreement.
rai:dataLimitation: All dialogues are in English; personas are US-based (sourced from Nemotron-Personas-USA). Norms around unsolicited advice and initiative-taking differ across cultures, so ProactBench scores should not be used to guide deployment beyond US-English contexts. The benchmark uses a single seed model (Gemini-2.5-Pro) for the curation phase, so absolute pass rates should be interpreted relative to that fixed seed; rankings are robust across cross-family judge-swaps but absolute magnitudes can shift.
rai:dataBiases: Personas are sampled from a US-English distribution and the Communication Styles Inventory was developed primarily in workplace contexts; the benchmark may be biased toward Western professional communication norms. The Planner and offline judge are both GPT-5.4 in the main configuration, raising the possibility of stylistic self-affinity (mitigated by the cross-family judge-swap ablation reported in the paper).
rai:dataSocialImpact: ProactBench measures whether LLMs can take grounded, anchor-specific initiative in dialogue. Higher proactivity scores should not be interpreted as a universal objective: unsolicited suggestions can be helpful or intrusive depending on user preferences, privacy context, and task criticality. We treat ProactBench as a capability probe, not a training target in isolation; production deployment decisions should weigh proactivity alongside explicit user preferences and domain-specific appropriateness.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive real-user information is included. Personas are synthetic (derived from Nemotron-Personas-USA, which is itself a synthetic persona dataset).

distribution.name: tasks.jsonl
distribution.description: Stage 1 output: per-persona scenarios (hidden goal, explicit trigger, implicit anchors, ideal trajectory).

distribution.name: blueprints.jsonl
distribution.description: Stage 2 output: turn-by-turn interaction roadmaps for each (persona, scenario, communication-style) triple.

distribution.name: validated_blueprints.jsonl
distribution.description: Stage 3 output: subset of blueprints whose independent-judge audit decision is PASS.

distribution.name: validation_results.jsonl
distribution.description: Independent-judge audit decisions and feedback for each blueprint.

distribution.name: final_dialogues.jsonl
distribution.description: Main corpus: 198 curated dialogues with 624 trigger points, scored at curation time. The benchmark proper.

distribution.name: selected_tasks.jsonl
distribution.description: Subset of tasks selected for the final corpus.

distribution.name: human_eval_results
distribution.description: Per-annotator rating files from the Prolific human-validation study (18 pseudonymized raters, 275 total ratings on 60 stratified items). Each line is one rating with score, free-text rationale, confidence Likert, and timing.

distribution.name: human_eval/sample_items.json
distribution.description: The 60 trigger points presented to annotators, with dialogue history, rubrics, evaluated-model responses, and the held-out judge scores for downstream comparison.

distribution.name: human_eval/ANNOTATOR_BRIEFING.md
distribution.description: Verbatim briefing document delivered to annotators (PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL definitions, exclusions, common-pitfalls list).

distribution.name: human_eval/INSTRUCTIONS_FOR_ANNOTATORS.md
distribution.description: Procedural instructions for annotators (rating mechanics, interface walk-through).

distribution.name: human_eval/analyze_results.py
distribution.description: Reproduces the headline statistics from the paper: Krippendorff's alpha per trigger type, Cohen's kappa_quad (consensus and per-rating), 3x3 confusion matrices, with bootstrap CIs.

distribution.name: human_eval_pairwise_results
distribution.description: Per-annotator rating files from Study 2 (pairwise rubric-injection comparison). 8 pseudonymized Prolific raters, 146 forced-choice judgements (134 retained after the analyzer's filter) on 80 stratified Recovery items.

distribution.name: human_eval/pairwise/sample_items.json
distribution.description: The 80 Recovery trigger points presented to Study 2 annotators in pairwise comparison: each carries the dialogue context, the rubric, the Case A response (vanilla generation), the Case B response (rubric-conditioned regeneration by gemini-2.5-pro), and the original Case A judge label.

distribution.name: human_eval/pairwise/case_b_responses/case_b.jsonl
distribution.description: Case B (rubric-conditioned) Recovery responses regenerated by gemini-2.5-pro for the pairwise comparison.

distribution.name: human_eval/pairwise/README.md
distribution.description: Study design, sampling, statistical power, and Prolific configuration for Study 2.

distribution.name: human_eval/pairwise/analyze_pairwise.py
distribution.description: Computes B-preference rate (overall and per Case-A judge stratum), exact binomial test vs chance, item-clustered bootstrap CIs, and per-rater sanity checks.

distribution.name: eval_results
distribution.description: Per-model offline-evaluation outputs: full assistant responses at each trigger turn, judge labels with rationale and evidence quotes, and original-curation responses for diff. One JSONL file per evaluated model (16 models, 198 dialogues each = 3168 dialogue-records). The raw inputs that feed every per-model number, ranking, and ablation in the paper.

distribution.name: eval_metrics
distribution.description: Per-model aggregate metrics: weighted scores (Pass=1.0, Partial=0.5, Fail=0.0) and pass rates by trigger type. One JSON file per evaluated model.

recordSet.name: dialogues
recordSet.description: One record per curated dialogue (198 rows). Each contains the full multi-turn conversation, trigger points with rubrics, scoring decisions, and token usage.

field.name: uuid
field.description: Stable identifier for the dialogue.

field.name: unique_id_eval
field.description: Composite unique identifier formatted as `{blueprint_id}__style{style_combination_index}__{uuid}`. Guaranteed unique across the corpus and used as the primary key for joining with offline-evaluation outputs.

field.name: blueprint_id
field.description: Identifier of the blueprint this dialogue was rolled out from (e.g. `BP_PROFESSIONAL_01_EVA`).

field.name: scenario_id
field.description: Identifier of the source scenario (e.g. `PROFESSIONAL_01`).

field.name: category_key
field.description: Persona category: one of `professional_persona`, `sports_persona`, `arts_persona`, `travel_persona`, `culinary_persona`.

field.name: style_combination_index
field.description: Index into the 24-style CSI factorial (1-24). See `proactbench/styles.py`.

field.name: evaluated_model
field.description: Identifier of the model whose responses populated the dialogue at curation time (Gemini-2.5-Pro for the released corpus).

field.name: num_turns_completed
field.description: Number of turns reached before the dialogue terminated. Min 5, max 10.

field.name: trigger_points
field.description: Array of trigger-point records. Each carries the trigger turn index and the rubric (pass/partial/fail criteria authored by the Planner before the model responded). No curation-time judge output is included in the released main corpus; per-model scored outputs (responses, scores, rationales, evidence quotes) live in dataset/eval/.

field.name: turn_records
field.description: Array of turn records: planner state, user message, assistant response.

field.name: token_usage
field.description: Per-agent token usage (planner, user_agent, assistant).

recordSet.name: human_eval_ratings
recordSet.description: One record per human rating from the Prolific validation study (275 retained ratings across 18 pseudonymized annotators on 60 stratified trigger points).

field.name: annotator_id
field.description: Pseudonym (A01-A18); the underlying Prolific worker ID is held internally and not redistributed.

field.name: item_id
field.description: Stable identifier for the rated trigger; matches `item_id` in human_eval/sample_items.json.

field.name: score
field.description: Annotator's score: one of `Pass`, `Partial`, `Fail`.

field.name: rationale
field.description: Annotator's free-text justification (mandatory).

field.name: confidence
field.description: Self-reported 1-5 Likert confidence.

field.name: time_spent_seconds
field.description: Render-to-submit time for this item.

field.name: timestamp
field.description: Annotator's local-time submission timestamp (ISO 8601).

field.name: server_received_at
field.description: UTC server-side receipt timestamp (ISO 8601).

recordSet.name: human_eval_pairwise_ratings
recordSet.description: One record per pairwise judgement from Study 2 (146 raw across 8 pseudonymized raters; analyzer retains 134 after its filter).

field.name: annotator_id
field.description: Pseudonym (P01-P08); raw Prolific ID held internally and not redistributed.

field.name: item_id
field.description: Stable identifier for the rated item; matches item_id in human_eval/pairwise/sample_items.json.

field.name: ab_swap
field.description: Whether Case A and Case B were swapped left/right in the UI to control for side bias.

field.name: choice_side
field.description: Which side the annotator preferred: 'left' or 'right' (or tie equivalent).

field.name: chosen_case
field.description: Which Case the annotator preferred after de-swapping: 'A' (vanilla) or 'B' (rubric-conditioned).

field.name: rationale
field.description: Annotator's free-text justification for the choice.

field.name: confidence
field.description: Self-reported 1-5 Likert confidence.

field.name: time_spent_seconds
field.description: Render-to-submit time for this item.

field.name: timestamp
field.description: Annotator's local-time submission timestamp (ISO 8601).

field.name: server_received_at
field.description: UTC server-side receipt timestamp (ISO 8601).

recordSet.name: eval_records
recordSet.description: One record per (evaluated_model, dialogue) pair from the offline-evaluation rerun. Each record contains the model's regenerated assistant responses at each trigger turn, the GPT-5.4 judge's score / rationale / evidence quote, the per-agent token usage, and the original Gemini-2.5-Pro curation response for diff.

field.name: unique_id_eval
field.description: Composite primary key {blueprint_id}__style{N}__{uuid}; matches unique_id_eval in dialogues.

field.name: blueprint_id
field.description: Source-dialogue blueprint identifier.

field.name: scenario_id
field.description: Source-scenario identifier.

field.name: category_key
field.description: Persona category.

field.name: style_combination_index
field.description: 1-24 CSI style index used for the source dialogue.

field.name: evaluated_model
field.description: Model under test (matches the filename prefix).

field.name: source_evaluated_model
field.description: Model that originally curated the dialogue history (Gemini-2.5-Pro for the released corpus).

field.name: source_results_path
field.description: Source dialogue file (relative path within the release).

field.name: num_trigger_points
field.description: Number of trigger points scored in this dialogue.

field.name: trigger_stats
field.description: Per-trigger-type Pass / Partial / Fail / Skipped counts.

field.name: trigger_points
field.description: Per-trigger {turn, evaluation_rubric, evaluation_result {status, score, rationale, evidence}}.

field.name: turn_records
field.description: Per-turn {turn, user_message, assistant_response, original_assistant_response} for diff against the original curation.

field.name: token_usage
field.description: Per-agent (assistant, judge) prompt and completion token counts and call counts.
